<ConflictType>No conflict — All retrieved documents agree that .com domains do not have an inherent SEO advantage over other TLDs.

The evidence clusters around a single, consistent claim: d1, d2, d3, d4, and d5 all state that Google treats all non-local domain extensions equally and that .com is not a ranking factor [d1, d2, d3, d4, d5]. Differences are superficial, such as d1 focusing on .STORE as an example and d2/d5 comparing .com to .net, but the core SEO principle is the same.

All documents support the answer that a .com domain is not better for SEO. d1, d2, d3, d4, and d5 collectively provide a decisive, unanimous answer by citing Google's stated policy that all non-local TLDs are treated the same, making abstention unnecessary.

No, a .COM domain is not better for SEO. Multiple sources state that Google treats all non-local top-level domains (TLDs) equally and that the domain extension itself is not a ranking factor [d1, d2, d3, d4]. For instance, Google has stated on record that they treat all domain extensions the same, so you won't get penalized for not having a .com [d1]. While .com may be preferred for branding and consumer trust [d5], from a pure SEO perspective, there is no inherent advantage over other extensions like .net, .io, or industry-specific TLDs [d2, d5]. Your overall SEO strategy is far more important than the choice of domain extension [d2].
